Help & Self-Serve Guide

You’re in the bay. Now what?

The Golffice is self-serve and open 24/7 — here’s everything you need to power up, play, and close out on your own.

Welcome! Every bay is self-serve and open 24/7. When you book, we text and email you a door code and your bay assignment. Walk in, find your bay, and the TrackMan simulator is ready to go. This guide walks you through the whole thing — getting in, powering up, picking a course, and closing out when you’re done. Stuck at any point? Call or text (205) 810-2245, day or night.
The door unlocks with the access code from your booking confirmation (check your text or email). Punch it into the keypad at the main entrance, then head to your assigned bay. Codes go live a few minutes before your session and expire when it ends. No code? Text or call (205) 810-2245 and we’ll get you in.
Power it up. The PC tower is in the cabinet beside the hitting mat — press the power button once and give it about a minute to boot. The projector wakes automatically. If it doesn’t, grab the small remote on the bay desk and press power once.
That’s just the projector asleep. Point the projector remote (on the bay desk) at the screen and press power once — give it 20–30 seconds to warm up. If the desktop shows on the computer but not the big screen, press “Source” on the remote until the golf software appears.
You’re in warm-up mode. On the TrackMan touchscreen, tap the menu (top-left), choose Play → On Course, then pick your course and tee and hit Start Round. You’re on the first tee. The range is always there when you want to loosen up before you play.
Easy fix. On the touchscreen, tap the menu and select End Round (confirm yes), then start fresh with Play → On Course. Whatever the last guest left behind won’t affect your session once you begin a new round.
On the setup screen you’ll choose: players and names, tee boxes (forward tees are more fun for beginners), gimme distance, and handicap on/off. You can also toggle mulligans. Ten seconds here and the round runs smoothly for the whole group.
Thousands — Augusta National, Pebble Beach, St. Andrews, Pinehurst No. 2 and many more. On the touchscreen, tap Play → On Course and use the search bar or filters to find a specific course. If it’s in the list, it’s ready to play right now.
Stroke Play, Match Play, Scramble, Best Ball, and Alternate Shot are all built in — pick your format on the round-setup screen. Solo? Stroke play is the classic. Big group? Scramble keeps everyone moving.
Absolutely. Choose a team format like Scramble, Best Ball, or Alternate Shot during setup, then assign players to teams. Perfect for date night or 2-on-2 with friends.
Nine times out of ten it’s ball placement — set the ball on the marked spot on the mat so the sensor can read it. Still stuck? Tap the menu → Restart Software, or fully reboot the PC (power button, wait a minute). If it’s really being stubborn, call (205) 810-2245 anytime.
The HUD shows your shot data: carry and total distance, ball speed, launch angle, spin, and shot shape. Up top you’ll see the hole layout, par, and distance to the pin; the mini-map shows where your ball landed. You don’t need any of it to have fun — but it’s there when you want to dial in your swing.
Aim first. Use the on-screen aim arrows (or drag on the touchscreen) to set your target line before you swing. Then just hit it there — the simulator reads your real club path and face, so line your body up toward where you want the ball to go.
We’ve all been there. If mulligans are enabled, tap “Mulligan” (or “Retry Shot”) on the touchscreen to wipe that swing and hit again. You can turn mulligans on anytime in the round settings. What happens in the bay stays in the bay.
Wrap up in three steps: (1) tap the menu → End Round so the bay’s clear for the next guest, (2) grab your clubs, drinks, and belongings, and (3) leave the computer and projector on — they reset on their own. The door locks behind you. That’s it — come back any time, day or night.

Marketing Bible

A creative proposal and brand opportunity overview

Confidential · Version 7.0 · thegolffice.com

A Note On This Document

You hired me to make a commercial.

You also hired me to audit the website and tighten things up. That work is in here. But while I was doing it I kept noticing things — opportunities in the positioning, gaps in the visual identity, a membership program without a name, a customer segment nobody in this category is talking to.

So I wrote them down.

Nothing in this document is a prescription. The Golffice works. The business model is solid. What follows is a menu — take what resonates, leave what does not, and let's talk about the rest.

The one thing I would ask for a green light on before anything else: the color system. It costs nothing to implement and it is the single change that would make every piece of creative — including the commercial — look like a real brand.

"The orange is doing real damage to the perceived price point. One commercial in the right palette changes that immediately."
The GolfficeConfidential

Who We Are

The strategic foundation — what The Golffice is, who it serves, and what makes it different from every competitor in the category.

01 · Who We AreThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

The Golffice is an upscale indoor golf simulator venue with locations across Alabama, Tennessee, and Kentucky. Open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, no tee time required.

"Something to do. No planning required."

The Strategic Center Of The Brand

We exist for one reason: to give people something fun to do. It is raining outside. It is January. You have a group of friends and nowhere to be. You want to do something different — something more interesting than another bar, another restaurant, another night on the couch. That is our customer, and that is our moment.

The Planet Fitness Of Indoor Golf

The Back Nine says up your game. We say just show up. A place where anyone can walk in, pick up a club, and play Augusta National without a lesson, a tee time, or a set of clubs in their car.

The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
02 · The Strategic InsightThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

The customer did not plan this.

They are not the serious golfer who blocked Tuesday at 7 PM to practice their swing. They are a group of people who looked out the window, saw rain, and started texting. They are coworkers looking for a team outing that does not feel like a team outing. They are couples who want something to do that is more interesting than dinner.

"This is a spontaneous, recreational, social activity. The triggers are weather, boredom, and the availability of friends. Our job is to be the obvious answer when someone asks what do we do tonight."

The Unlock — House Clubs

The casual recreational customer is the largest and least served segment in the indoor golf category. And the single biggest barrier to a spontaneous visit is simple: nobody in the group has clubs in the car. The House Club program removes that barrier entirely. A group of four people on a rainy Saturday can now walk in on impulse. That is the conversion moment.

House Club smart locker system — "Clubs available at every bay. Just show up."

The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
03

Who We're Talking To

Three distinct audience segments, each with different triggers and different conversion paths — but one shared characteristic: they are looking for something fun to do.

03 · AudienceThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

Primary — The Casual Social Group

Two to four people, mixed gender, ages 25 to 50, looking for something fun to do together. They may or may not play golf. They do not own clubs or if they do they are not in the car. Driven by a spontaneous decision — weather, a free evening, a group text that went somewhere. The highest-volume, highest-growth segment in the indoor golf category and almost entirely unaddressed by the competition.

Secondary — The Recreational Regular

Someone who plays golf occasionally or used to play and wants to stay connected to the game. Appreciates the technology but is not here to analyze data. Comes in a few times a month and brings different people with them every time. The word-of-mouth engine.

Tertiary — The Corporate And Events Client

A decision-maker booking an experience for a group. Team outing, client entertainment, birthday, bachelor party. The Golffice works for mixed skill levels in the same bay at the same time — that is the key differentiator for this segment.

The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
04

The Character

An internal creative methodology that gives the brand a consistent personality across every touchpoint — copy, color, photography, advertising.

04 · The CharacterThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

What Is Character Brand?

Character Brand is a strategic methodology that treats a brand as a character, not a story. Instead of defining values and tone guides in the abstract, we find one specific, fully realized person — real or fictional — whose personality already embodies everything the brand should be. That person becomes the creative compass.

The character is never mentioned publicly. The brand does not say it was built around Ty Webb. The character informs everything and appears in nothing. What the public sees is a brand with a coherent personality — they just do not know why it feels that way.

Cast
Ty Webb
Caddyshack, 1980
The best golfer at Bushwood Country Club and the only one who does not care about that. Effortlessly skilled, philosophically detached from competition. Charming without performing charm. Dry, unhurried, warm. He already thinks you belong here.
"You don't have to be good at golf to love golf."  "Book the bay. Bring the crew."  "The course doesn't care if it's raining. Neither do we."  "Just show up."
The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
05

Brand Color Palette

Four colors. Locked. The single most important takeaway from this document — and the one thing that costs nothing to implement immediately.

05 · Color Palette — Final / LockedThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

The current palette — dark green and orange — reads generic. Every indoor golf venue uses the same visual language. The palette below was derived directly from The Golffice's own physical space and locked as of July 2026.

#76ABAE
Steel Teal
Primary Brand Color
The anchor. Nobody in indoor golf owns this color. That is the point.
#303841
Dark Charcoal
Base / Backgrounds
More refined than navy, warmer than pure black. Premium and grounded.
#FF5722
Burnt Sienna
CTA / Accent / Energy
Every Book a Bay button. Every offer. The personality color of the brand.
#F5F5F5
Off White
Type / Light Backgrounds
Clean and warm. Never use pure white — it reads cold against the palette.

Hard Rules

  • Never use orange as a decorative element — Burnt Sienna is CTA only
  • Never use pure white — always Off White #F5F5F5
  • Never use bright green — every golf brand already lives there
  • Every CTA button across all touchpoints is Burnt Sienna #FF5722 — no exceptions
The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
06 · Voice And ToneThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

The Nevers

  • Never say "Up your game" or "Improve your swing"
  • Never say "Rain or Shine" or "No matter the weather"
  • Never use urgency language — Book Now, Don't Miss Out
  • Never talk down to the non-golfer
  • Never lead with technology specs
  • Never make the customer feel like they need to plan

The Always

  • Always assume the customer already belongs here
  • Always speak to the spontaneous decision
  • Always lead with the social experience, not the golf
  • Always make no-clubs-needed feel like a feature
  • Always sound like you have nowhere else to be

Tagline

"The course is always open."

Leading Candidate

  • "Just show up." — The most direct expression of the brand promise.
  • "Rain outside. Course inside." — Speaks directly to the spontaneous occasion.
  • "Book the bay. Bring the crew." — Social group conversion line.
The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026

08 · Competitive PositioningThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

The Planet Fitness move.

Planet Fitness did not try to out-muscle Gold's Gym. They talked to everyone who was intimidated by Gold's Gym, removed the judgment, and became one of the fastest-growing fitness chains in history. The Golffice makes the same move in indoor golf.

Photography Direction

  • Casual clothing always — jeans, hoodies, sneakers. The customer should see themselves.
  • Groups over individuals — this is a social activity, show it that way.
  • Simulator screens must be vivid and show recognizable world-famous courses.
  • Dark walls and modern surfaces only — clean, upscale entertainment venue aesthetic.

11

Business Opportunities

Two self-funding revenue programs — House Clubs and manufacturer trials — that reinforce the casual positioning and add $1,700 to $3,500+ per location every month, with almost no operational overhead.

11 · Business Opportunity — House ClubsThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

House Club Program

Not an amenity — the operational unlock that makes the whole casual positioning possible. A group on a rainy Saturday doesn't have clubs in the car. They weren't planning this. House Clubs turn a spontaneous idea into a booked session.

A bowling alley doesn't make you bring your own ball. A pool hall doesn't make you bring your own cue. The Golffice shouldn't make you bring your own clubs.

Projected Impact

  • 15–25% lift in first-time walk-in conversion
  • Corporate & event bookings rise — planners can't ask attendees to bring gear
  • ~20% more bookings within 90 days (conservative)

Self-Service · Zero Staff

  • Smart lockers, a unique PIN texted at session start
  • Weight sensors confirm return — auto card charge after 30 min
  • RFID tags + door sensor make theft nearly impossible

Revenue Math

  • $15 × 20 rentals/wk = $1,200 gross
  • Less $200 wear = $1,000 net / location / month
  • $4,000–6,500 capital · ~90-day payback

"Clubs available at every bay. Just show up." — the single most important line in casual-market conversion. Website hero, every social ad, every event package.

The GolfficeConfidential · July 2026
11 · Business Opportunity — Try Before You BuyThe Golffice · Marketing Bible

Try Before You Buy

A captive audience of recreational golfers in a high-engagement moment — holding a club, making shot decisions, emotionally invested. One of the most valuable product-trial environments in all of golf. Manufacturers will pay for access to it.

National Manufacturer Partnerships

  • Rotate featured sets quarterly — Callaway, TaylorMade, Cleveland, Cobra, Ping
  • Equipment provided free, or a $500–$2,000 placement fee per location per quarter
  • TrackMan & Uneekor data pre-sells — customers who watch their numbers improve are sold before they reach a store
  • QR code links to the product page or retailer — zero staff

Local Pro Shop Partnerships

  • Referral deal or a flat $200–$500 / month visibility fee
  • Demo days — retailer brings new arrivals for dedicated sessions
  • Bundled offers — "Buy a set, get a free bay rental"
  • Gift-card cross-promotion driving traffic both directions
